voices.note: ת"ר (31a.17): one who prays must direct his heart toward Heaven

props.gloss_en: one who prays must direct his heart toward Heaven
Abba Shaul: a sign for the matter -- 'You direct their heart, Your ear listens' (Ps 10:17)
this was R' Akiva's custom: when he prayed with the congregation he would shorten and go up
because of the burden on the congregation
and when he prayed by himself, a person would leave him in one corner and find him in another
and why all this? because of bowings and prostrations

supports.gloss_en: סימן לדבר: תכין לבם תקשיב אזנך -- a sign, not a proof: where the heart is directed, the ear listens
מפני טורח ציבור -- he shortened so as not to burden the congregation
וכל כך למה? מפני כריעות והשתחוויות
